purpose: Reconstruct how the IJA's already-existing 1943 anti-tank development policy is changed by GALVANIC M4 contact, Bengal Lee/Grant contact, and Branch success of the Chi-Ha family.

1943_07_research_policy.state: IJA armor development had already shifted toward anti-tank combat before GALVANIC.
1943_07_research_policy.ChiTo: 1942H2 new-medium program; July 1943 requirement moved from 47mm-class toward long 57mm and heavier protection.
1943_07_research_policy.ChiRi: July 1943 research-policy line included a 75mm-class heavier medium-tank requirement.
1943_07_research_policy.meaning: Tarawa/Bengal do not invent the concept of a 75mm anti-tank tank. They change urgency, procurement priority, and the need for a stopgap.

ChiHe.historical_mass_production: 1944 spring; commonly reconstructed factory output begins Feb 1944
ChiHe.role: better 5-man/radio/armor/engine system but 47mm remains inadequate as a reliable frontal answer to M4-class armor

ChiNu_historical.architecture: Chi-He lineage hull + new large turret + Type 3 75mm tank gun derived from the existing Type 90 75mm field gun

HoNiI_Type90.state: Existing practical architecture before 1944: Type97 chassis + Type90 75mm field gun; Type90 was also recognized as usable in an anti-tank role.
HoNiI_Type90.importance: This gives the IJA a faster 75mm mobile-firepower path than waiting for a new turreted medium tank.

GALVANIC.information: High confidence that US 75mm medium tanks materially improve assault reduction power; detailed Japanese post-battle exploitation is poor because the garrison is destroyed/isolated.
GALVANIC.effect: Immediate warning that the 47mm/light-tank system does not provide a comfortable frontal answer.

BENGAL.contact_state: 25th Dragoons Lee/Grant reinforcement is route-disrupted by loss of Ukhia access, Japanese old-battleship bombardment, Karnaphuli crossings and British demolitions; only small packets are likely to fight.
BENGAL.effect: Surviving divisional/army communications can report that 30-ton 75mm British medium tanks are physically present in the India-Burma theater.

European_global_intelligence.effect: The technical establishment already knows that world medium-tank design is moving toward heavier armor and 75mm-class guns. Branch decision does not require perfect Tiger/Panther/Sherman blueprints.

branch_intelligence_fusion.fused_message_to_Tokyo: The problem is not a local Tarawa anomaly. Allied 30-ton/75mm medium armor is becoming a recurring threat in both Pacific amphibious warfare and the India-Burma theater.

branch_decision_gate.centered_result: YES: urgent anti-Allied-medium-tank program is opened.
reasoning: July-1943 anti-tank policy means the bureaucracy already accepts the technical direction.
Bengal gives an independent theater warning with a surviving reporting chain.
Branch armor reliability makes tank forces institutionally more credible, strengthening the case for investment.
Aircraft/ship/shipping priorities still prevent a large national tank-production surge.

track_A_immediate_field_solution.name: 75mm direct-fire / Ho-Ni anti-tank reserve
actions: Issue doctrine emphasizing mines/immobilization, flank geometry, and concealed 75mm direct fire against Allied medium tanks.
Reserve AP ammunition and selected motorized Type90 75mm field guns for armored/anti-tank contingency roles.
Reclassify existing Ho-Ni I vehicles as valuable anti-medium-tank mobile reserve assets rather than only mobile artillery.
Place a small follow-on Ho-Ni-I-type 75mm batch or equivalent production restart under urgent study/order.
track_A_immediate_field_solution.guard: Type90 field guns are scarce and useful as artillery; do not strip China/Bengal field artillery wholesale.

track_B_ChiHe_acceleration.name: Bring Chi-He production forward modestly
track_B_ChiHe_acceleration.historical_problem: Design already complete; production lag is substantially a priority/tooling/resource problem rather than ignorance of how to build the vehicle.
track_B_ChiHe_acceleration.branch_change: Advance line switchover by roughly 2-5 weeks, not by a year.
track_B_ChiHe_acceleration.deployment: school, proving, depot and selected home/armored-formation conversion only; no overseas combat unit centered by 21 Feb
track_B_ChiHe_acceleration.opportunity_cost: Shinhoto tail and other vehicle work lose roughly 8-15 medium-chassis-equivalent slots through Feb; no extra national hull magic.

track_C_75mm_stopgap_medium.name: Chi-He-lineage 75mm turreted stopgap
track_C_75mm_stopgap_medium.historical_analogue: This is the causal ancestor of a Chi-Nu-like solution, but its final Branch designation/layout is not frozen yet.
track_C_75mm_stopgap_medium.design_choice: Use a Chi-He-lineage hull and adapt the existing Type90 75mm ballistic family into a tank installation; use a new turret rather than wait for Chi-To.

1944_02_21_state.layout_trade: CLOSED centered: turreted stopgap beats a new 25-30t hull for near-term production

prototype_clock.reason: Historical May->Sep development took about four months; Branch has earlier start, better compute/metrology/QC and existing Ho-Ni/Type90 integration experience, but turret/ring/recoil/sight/manufacturing work remains physical.

production_gate.earliest_low_rate: 1944-05 late if trials go unusually well
production_gate.not_yet_granted: No quantity or Marianas shipment is booked at this stage.

track_D_ChiTo_long_term.name: Skip treating 57mm Chi-To as the future production answer
track_D_ChiTo_long_term.branch_change: The 57mm prototype may still be completed as a chassis/test article because sunk work exists, but the production requirement is frozen around a 75mm-class main armament earlier than the historical final redesign.
track_D_ChiTo_long_term.1944_02_21_state: new-hull development continues; 75mm turret/gun path receives higher design priority, but engine, hull, armor and large-turret manufacturing remain major gates.
track_D_ChiTo_long_term.effect: Potentially saves a later redesign cycle; does not create a usable 30t tank in 1944H1.

rejected_or_secondary_paths.mass_ChiHe_as_M4_killer: REJECTED. Better tank system, wrong main-gun class for reliable frontal M4 combat.
rejected_or_secondary_paths.HoI_short_75mm_as_primary_AT_answer: SECONDARY. Useful HE/fire support and close ambush possibilities, but low-velocity 75mm is not the preferred medium-tank counter.
rejected_or_secondary_paths.crash_ChiRi_or_heavy_tank: REJECTED for near term because engines, armor plate, transport, factories and time dominate.
rejected_or_secondary_paths.abandon_Shinhoto: REJECTED. 47mm Shinhoto remains highly cost-effective in China, Burma/South and against lighter armor; it becomes theater/role differentiated rather than obsolete everywhere.

content: 47mm: avoid centered frontal duel with Allied 30t medium tanks; seek side/rear, short range, prepared lanes.
37mm/light tanks: reconnaissance, flank/mobile firepoint and infantry-support roles; no frontal medium-tank duel.
75mm field/SPG: concealed direct-fire anti-tank reserve where terrain permits.
mines/engineers/artillery: immobilize and channel before direct-fire engagement.
tank units: preserve reliable Chi-Ha/Shinhoto mobility for local counterattack rather than sacrificial frontal charge.
doctrine_output_by_1944_02_21.distribution: Tank School / artillery-school / selected formation guidance can circulate during Jan-Feb; theater adoption remains local.

industrial_effect_by_1944_02_21.steel: No national tank steel surge. Branch 1944 industry is healthier than historical but aircraft, ships, merchant shipping and trucks remain competing priorities.
industrial_effect_by_1944_02_21.engine: 240hp Type100-class engine production becomes a more explicit bottleneck because Chi-He and the stopgap share the improved chassis lineage.
industrial_effect_by_1944_02_21.guns: 75mm gun/breech/recoil/sight throughput is the most important near-term stopgap bottleneck.
industrial_effect_by_1944_02_21.turret: Large rotating turret manufacturing is the main difference between an immediate Ho-Ni-type solution and a later Chi-Nu-like solution.
industrial_effect_by_1944_02_21.net: By Feb21 the qualitative decision has changed, but fielded tank strength has not yet changed dramatically.

retroactive_implications.China_pre_GALVANIC: Mostly quantity/serviceability/model-mix corrections; no 75mm stopgap back-port.
retroactive_implications.Bengal_Dec1943: Reopen Lee/Grant contact and existing Japanese AT/vehicle balance, but no Jan1944 production response can be back-ported into the December battle.
retroactive_implications.GALVANIC: No new Japanese weapons added; it is an intelligence/requirement trigger.
retroactive_implications.post_Feb1944: Every tank-sensitive campaign must use the new production/development clocks.

next_gates: Rebuild Bengal 2-15 Dec armored contact only enough to fix the quality of the Lee/Grant report and wreck-exploitation gate.
Then determine what is physically accepted, assigned, shipped and delivered before Marianas; do not decide Saipan first.
